The component initializes `isStandalone` to `false`, causing it to render `null` on initial mount. In `useEffect`, `__dismissHardSkeleton()` is called synchronously before React processes the `setIsStandalone(standalone)` state update and mounts `<TabijiSplashAnimation />`. Additionally, `__dismissHardSkeleton()` is invoked before checking `hasShown || !standalone`. This tears down the static hard skeleton 1-2 frames before the animated splash component can be rendered and painted by the browser, resulting in a flash of unhydrated/bare DOM.
findings.remediation_hint: Do not invoke `__dismissHardSkeleton()` synchronously in the mount `useEffect` when standalone splash animation is going to be displayed. Instead, only invoke `__dismissHardSkeleton()` immediately if `hasShown || !standalone`. When showing the splash animation, defer dismissal until `TabijiSplashAnimation` signals its first painted frame via an `onReady` callback or after `requestAnimationFrame`.
